title: Yasujirō Ozu
idiom: Gorey ink with Japanese woodblock influence — spare crosshatching, deep shadow, a single still domestic scene (a corridor, a low tatami room, an empty hallway) as if seen from the tatami-level camera position, no figures, only the space they left behind
hero_prompt: Wide darkened backdrop in the register of Edward Gorey ink crosshatching fused with Edo-period Japanese woodblock print: a low tatami-level view down a long empty corridor, sliding shoji screens casting grid shadows, a single vase with one bare branch, the composition perfectly still and slightly off-center, deep blacks with spare white, no letters, numerals, words, labels — purely pictorial
icon_prompt: Bold high-contrast square emblem: a tatami-level camera lens rendered as a circle, behind it the silhouette of a low doorframe with shoji grid, stark black on white in Gorey ink style, no fine linework at small scale — every element readable at 24px, no letters, numerals, words, labels — purely pictorial
